title: $TRUMP meme coin
summary: Trump launched the official $TRUMP meme coin on the evening of January 17, 2025, about 2.5 days before his inauguration. His own 2025 OGE financial disclosure reports about $635-636M in meme-coin royalty and licensing income through CIC Digital LLC, so the '$600M' figure is a slight understatement of self-reported gross income. TRUMP (about 95% down in early 2026, about 98% by November 2026) and MELANIA (about 99% down) have collapsed, and on-chain data shows most buyers lost money, though no exact share exists. Trump did make the 'lead or China takes over' remark (CNBC, July 2026). The suggestion that he launched the coin 'so China wouldn't do it first' is the video's sarcastic paraphrase.

sub_claims.statement: Trump launched an official meme coin two days before taking office.
sub_claims.finding: Announced on Truth Social and X on the evening of Friday, Jan 17, 2025 (Jan 18 UTC); inauguration Jan 20. CIC Digital LLC and Fight Fight Fight LLC held 80% of the supply, locked and vesting over three years; 200M of the planned 1B tokens were released at launch.

sub_claims.statement: The president raked in $600 million from the Trump coin.
sub_claims.finding: The 2025 OGE disclosure (released 2026-06-30) lists 'Celebration Coins' royalties of $635,068,835 via CIC Digital LLC (about $636.1M on the CIC Digital licensing and crypto line). This is gross licensing income Trump reported himself. Earlier outside estimates ranged from about $315M (Forbes) to more than $800M (Conor Grogan).

sub_claims.statement: Money flowed through shell companies, which Molly White tracked.
sub_claims.finding: Proceeds flow through LLCs: CIC Digital LLC (a Trump Organization affiliate) and Fight Fight Fight LLC (run by Bill Zanker). 'Shell companies' is a pejorative label. Molly White's Citation Needed newsletter analyzed the disclosure; her specific entity tracking was not independently located.

sub_claims.statement: Melania reported $6 million on her coin and NFTs.
sub_claims.finding: The 2025 OGE filing shows more than $6M from NFTs and 'other collectibles' under a Designers Manager license. The filing does not name $MELANIA; linking the income to the coin is an analyst inference (CAP).

sub_claims.statement: Asked about his family's crypto, Trump said the US must be at the top or China will take it over.
sub_claims.finding: In a White House interview with CNBC's Joe Kernen around July 2, 2026, Trump said he 'could know' about the ventures but didn't, called them 'nothing illegal,' and said the US must lead or 'China's going to take it over.' He was talking about crypto generally, not giving a reason for the meme coin.

sub_claims.statement: TRUMP has lost about 95% of its value; MELANIA about 99%.
sub_claims.finding: TRUMP peaked at about $73.43 on 2025-01-19. It was about 95% down in early 2026 and about 98% down (about $1.05-1.10) by Nov 9-13, 2026. MELANIA peaked at about $13.73 and is about 99% down.

sub_claims.statement: Buyers, unless very early, have almost exclusively lost money.
sub_claims.finding: In May 2025 Chainalysis data (via CNBC) showed about 764,000 of roughly 2M buyer wallets at a loss, while 58 wallets made more than $10M each (about $1.1B combined). Prices have fallen much further since. Retail losses across TRUMP and MELANIA are estimated at about $4.3B. Wallet counts are not people, and no exact share of losing buyers exists.

corrections: Transcript says 'two days' before taking office; the launch was the evening of Jan 17, 2025 (ET), about 2.5 days before the Jan 20 inauguration.
Transcript says $600M; Trump's own 2025 disclosure reports about $635-636M in gross meme-coin royalty and licensing income via CIC Digital.
Transcript says TRUMP is down about 95%; that was accurate in early 2026, but by November 2026 it was about 98% below its peak.
The China remark was about crypto generally (CNBC, July 2026), not a stated reason for launching the meme coin.
denials_and_context: Trump said on Truth Social that the coin was not intended to be an investment opportunity.

The White House says Trump's assets are held in a trust managed by his children and that ethics rules are followed. Trump told CNBC it is 'nothing illegal' and that Eric Trump and outside managers run the businesses.
The income figures come from Trump's self-reported gross licensing income, not audited profit. Estimates from other methods range from about $315M to more than $800M.
Critics, including the WSJ editorial board, called the arrangement an 'unseemly display of using the Presidency for family profit.'
